solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Underworld girls in sacks

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and a name for the underworld itself
misses are young unmarried women

explanation.surface: A grim picture of young women stuffed into sacks in the land of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack someone is to fire them from a job, which is what dismissal means.

clue.text: Fellow's love with doom around

indicators.note: doom's synonym is placed round the letter for love, enclosing it

parts.note: to damn someone is to doom them to perdition
love is nil in tennis scoring, shown as the letter O

explanation.surface: A man whose sweetheart is surrounded by impending doom.
explanation.walkthrough: Damon, of the legendary friends Damon and Pythias, is simply a man's name here; the 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Damon is a man's first name, so a fellow can be called Damon in a crossword.

clue.text: Paper's fund for something relatively dark

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper; with the possessive it gives SUNS
a pot is a pool of money collected for some purpose

explanation.surface: A newspaper's money set aside for something shady.
explanation.definitionFit: A solar blemish looks dark only by comparison with the brighter surface of the star around it.

clue.text: Not "tearing apart", one's gathered!

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: the words are pulled apart and their letters reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: An exclamation that someone is being drawn in rather than torn to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: I for 'one' plus NOT TEARING broken 'apart' (NTEGRATION) gives the answer; the whole clue also describes it, since bringing together is the opposite of tearing apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing separate elements together into a whole is the opposite of ripping something into pieces.

clue.text: Scotch or soft drink?

definitions.meaning: to scotch a plan or rumour is to crush or suppress it
in Britain ... is a fruit cordial diluted with water

explanation.surface: A barman asking whether you want whisky or something non-alcoholic.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for crushing an idea and the British name for a dilutable fruit cordial.

clue.text: Rough leather: can it match calfskin, ultimately?

parts.note: 'can it!' is slang for shut up, as is 'sh'
to agree is to correspond or match

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of calfskin is used

explanation.surface: A leatherworker wondering whether coarse hide can compare with soft calfskin.
explanation.definitionFit: Shagreen is untanned leather with a granular, roughened surface, often made from sharkskin.

clue.text: Plant leaf half destroyed by insect

parts.note: a bug is an insect

indicators.note: half of the word leaf is destroyed, leaving its first two letters

explanation.surface: A garden plant whose leaf has been half eaten by a pest.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugle is a low-growing creeping plant of the mint family with blue flower spikes.

clue.text: False god inadequate? Cry

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: Baal was a Canaanite deity, condemned in the Bible as a false god

explanation.surface: Someone questioning whether an idol is lacking, then a shout.
explanation.definitionFit: Baa is the bleat a sheep makes, its characteristic call.

clue.text: Female relative has nothing with the Continental breakfast cereal

parts.note: gran is a grandmother
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
la is 'the' in French, a Continental language

explanation.surface: Grandma eats nothing but a European-style cereal for breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Granola is a breakfast mix of baked oats, nuts and honey.

clue.text: Ultimately nice and comfortable bit of shrub for biological set-up

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of nice

parts.note: cosy means snug and comfortable
a stem is a part of a shrub

explanation.surface: A pleasant snug sprig of bush serving some biological arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecosystem is a community of organisms interacting with their environment, a biological system.

clue.text: Force one to put in team

indicators.note: put in means placed inside the team's name

parts.note: Man U is the usual short name for Manchester United football club
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A manager compelling a player to be selected for the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' looks like a verb about compelling; it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Manitou is the Algonquian name for a spirit or supernatural power pervading nature.

clue.text: Native Americans here — gosh, a soldier is retreating!

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: oh is an exclamation of surprise, like gosh
a para is a paratrooper

explanation.surface: An exclamation of alarm as a soldier pulls back before Native warriors.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arapaho are a Native American people of the Great Plains.

clue.text: Small drink, peg, knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back suggests a drink downed but here means the word is reversed

parts.note: a pin is a peg

explanation.surface: A tot of spirits, a peg in Indian English, downed in one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' looks like drinking, matching the definition, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nip is a small measure of spirits.

clue.text: Actors get twitchy — heavens, there's a loss of stomach!

indicators.note: twitchy means jumpy and restless, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: 'my!' is an exclamation like 'heavens!'

explanation.surface: Nervous actors lose their nerve before going on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loss of stomach' suggests losing courage; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastrectomy is the surgical removal of all or part of the stomach.

clue.text: Cashew trees supply something to get your teeth into

definitions.text: something to get your teeth into

indicators.note: read as 'supple-y', meaning flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: Nut trees providing a solid snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is read as the adverb from supple, flexibly, not as a verb meaning provide.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheese straw is a crisp baked stick of cheesy pastry, a savoury snack you bite into.

clue.text: Hospital department facing rebuke for trick

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
a rap is a sharp reprimand

explanation.surface: A hospital unit facing criticism over a deception.
explanation.definitionFit: To trick someone into a situation is to ensnare them by cunning.

clue.text: Conveyor of tragedy in English university with final message before fateful day

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is the parting message on a gravestone
the Ides of March was the day Caesar was assassinated

explanation.surface: A tragic story told at an English university, with a last word before a doomed date.
explanation.definitionFit: Euripides was one of the three great Athenian writers of tragic drama.

clue.text: What may return to haunt woman, part of Bible introduced by cleric

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a cleric
Ena is a woman's name
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A clergyman leading in a woman and a scripture passage that may come back to trouble someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A revenant is a ghost or corpse that comes back from the dead.

clue.text: Feeling ecstatic about money, grabbing fortune finally

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the next piece

parts.note: sent is slang for transported with delight

indicators.note: grabbing means the money word takes hold of the letter that follows

parts.note: tin is old slang for money

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of fortune

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled by cash after landing a windfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentient being is one capable of feeling and perception, an adjective sense.

clue.text: Repaid and rather embarrassed about it

indicators.note: about means the colour word goes round the other piece

parts.note: red-faced with embarrassment
quite means rather or fairly

explanation.surface: Someone paid back and somewhat sheepish about the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to 'rather', the piece enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Requited love or a requited favour has been returned in kind.

clue.text: What some meetings need to be when Queen gets to speak

definitions.text: What some meetings need to be

parts.note: to orate is to make a speech

explanation.surface: The monarch addresses a meeting, which must have enough present.
explanation.definitionFit: A quorate meeting has the minimum attendance needed to do business validly.

clue.text: Like husband with memory going into retreat

parts.note: as means like
RAM is random access memory in computing

explanation.surface: A forgetful spouse heading off for a quiet getaway.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu religious retreat or hermitage.

clue.text: One mistake at the end of game somewhere in London

indicators.note: at the end of places the next pieces after the game abbreviation

parts.note: RU is rugby union
the Roman numeral for one is I
a slip is a small error

explanation.surface: A single blunder at the close of a match somewhere in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: RUISLIP is a suburb in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruislip is a district in the London Borough of Hillingdon, so a place in London.

clue.text: Shock maybe about old books offering nonsense

indicators.note: about means the hair word goes round the books

parts.note: a shock is a thick mass of hair
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A jolt about antique volumes offering rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' suggests surprise; here it is a shock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot air is empty, boastful talk with no substance.

clue.text: Revealing prominent feature of tough parson being unorthodox

indicators.note: unorthodox means not following the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rugged vicar with a striking face and odd views.
explanation.definitionFit: Prognathous describes a protruding jaw, a feature that juts forward on the face.

clue.text: Man needing a change of heart and belief

indicators.note: the central letter of the island's abbreviation is swapped for another

parts.note: IOM is the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A fellow who must change his mind and his convictions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, IOM; its middle letter O changes to S.
explanation.definitionFit: An ism is a doctrine or ideology, any system of thought.

clue.text: One of the old people with a refusal in the morning to get up

indicators.note: in a down clue getting up means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: nay is a word of refusal
a.m. means in the morning

explanation.surface: An elderly person who says no when told to rise early.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maya were an ancient Central American civilisation, so one of them belongs to an old people.

clue.text: Transport going back a few feet taking time

indicators.note: going back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a yard is three feet
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A vehicle reversing a short distance and taking its time.
explanation.definitionFit: Drayage is haulage of goods by cart or truck, a form of conveyance.

clue.text: Sacred box that housed survivors

definitions.meaning: the ... of the Covenant was the chest holding the tablets of the Law
Noah's vessel carried his family and animals through the Flood

explanation.surface: A holy chest that gave shelter to those who lived through some disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the biblical chest of the Covenant and Noah's boat.

clue.text: A very old city friend coming across in conversation?

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city in Mesopotamia
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A friend from an ancient city drops into a chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something conveyed in talk reaches the listener through the ears, by hearing.

clue.text: Cut interest you might pick up

indicators.note: picking up means hearing, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: a stake is a share or interest in something

explanation.surface: A reduced rate of interest that you might be able to get.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' and 'interest' suggest finance; it is a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A steak is a thick slice taken from a carcass, a cut of beef or fish.

clue.text: New form of power then made widely available

indicators.note: a new form of the words means their letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A fresh kind of energy then becoming accessible to all.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw something open is to make it accessible to everyone.
